info.short_name: Hepatitis C patients
info.long_name: Number of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis
info.short_description: Annual count of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.
info.long_description: Count of distinct Epic Cosmos patients with at least one encounter in the calendar year who carry a viral hepatitis C diagnosis, by state of residence and age at encounter. The population base is all patients with any encounter and Country of Care = United States of America; no diagnosis filter is applied to the population, and the diagnosis restriction is applied as a row-level bucket so that the all-patients denominator (epic_n_patients) is reported alongside it. The diagnosis bucket was defined in SlicerDicer as ICD-10-CM B18.2 (chronic viral hepatitis C), B19.2 (unspecified viral hepatitis C), B17.1 (acute hepatitis C), and B17.2 (acute hepatitis E) as of the predecessor session; this has not been independently re-verified against the current session (2855468). B17.2 is not a hepatitis C code, so these counts likely contain a small number of acute hepatitis E patients; the bucket definition should be corrected and the session re-exported. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic Cosmos and imputed as 5 here, flagged by epic_n_patients_hepc_suppressed_flag. The age value "Total" is the source's own overall-age total and includes patients whose age at encounter is unknown, so it exceeds the sum of the six age buckets by 1 to 2.5 percent; use the "Total" row for overall figures rather than summing the buckets. The most recent period may be a partial year, identifiable because its time value is not December 31 (currently 2026-08-18, covering January 1 to August 18 only). Counts for a partial period are NOT comparable to a full year. Use epic_pct_hepc for trend comparisons that include a partial period. As of the 2026-09-10 update (session 2855468), this series now covers 2018 onward with the age "Total" column throughout -- the earlier 2018-2019 NA gap from the predecessor session (2850163) is resolved. The underlying export also carries two additional measure columns per age bucket ("HepC diagnosis (%)" and a medication-within-6-months percentage) that are deliberately NOT captured here -- see ingest.R's CAVEAT comment for why.

A flag of 1 always accompanies the imputed value 5, and no source-reported value carries a flag of 1.

info.short_name: All patients
info.long_name: Number of patients with any encounter (denominator)
info.short_description: Annual count of all patients with any encounter, used as the hepatitis C denominator.
info.long_description: Count of distinct Epic Cosmos patients with at least one encounter in the calendar year, regardless of diagnosis, by state of residence and age at encounter. Taken from the per-state "Total" row of the diagnosis dimension in the SlicerDicer export, which includes all data under that state bucket. This is the denominator for epic_pct_hepc. Because it counts the full Epic Cosmos patient population rather than a census population, it reflects Epic's market share in each state and is not a general population count; state-to-state comparisons of the count itself are therefore not meaningful, though the derived percentage is comparable. The age value "Total" is the source's own overall-age total and includes patients of unknown age, so it exceeds the sum of the six buckets. Like the numerator, a count for a partial trailing period (time not ending December 31) covers only part of the year and is not comparable to a full year. Counts of 10 or fewer would be suppressed and imputed as 5; no denominator cell was suppressed in the current export.

info.short_name: Percent with hepatitis C
info.long_name: Percent of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis
info.short_description: Percent of patients with any encounter who have a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.
info.long_description: Derived as epic_n_patients_hepc / epic_n_patients * 100 within each geography, year, and age group. Because both numerator and denominator come from the same Epic Cosmos patient population, this percentage is comparable across states and years in a way the raw counts are not. It measures diagnosed hepatitis C among patients who sought care, not population prevalence, and so is sensitive to testing and care-seeking patterns as well as to Epic's coverage in each state. Where the numerator was suppressed (10 or fewer), the imputed numerator of 5 carries through, which is equivalent to the 5 / denominator * 100 imputation rule; those cells are flagged by epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag. Where the denominator was suppressed, the value is left missing instead of computing 5 / 5 = 100%. Because numerator and denominator cover the same window, this measure is far more robust to a partial trailing period than the raw counts are, though it is still not strictly comparable to a full year, since a shorter observation window gives each patient fewer opportunities for a diagnosis to be recorded. Nationally (geography "00", age "Total") the rate has declined steadily: 0.45% (2018), 0.45% (2019), 0.42% (2020), 0.39% (2021), 0.38% (2022), 0.37% (2023), 0.36% (2024), 0.34% (2025), with the 2026-08-18 partial period at 0.32%. The underlying diagnosis bucket also includes ICD-10-CM B17.2 (acute hepatitis E) in error - see epic_n_patients_hepc.

info.short_name: HCV medication rate among diagnosed
info.long_name: Percent of HCV-diagnosed patients who received an HCV medication within 6 months of diagnosis
info.short_description: Rate of medication initiation within 6 months among all patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.
info.long_description: Taken directly from the medication crosstab's own rate column (imputed via the standard 5 / denominator rule when blank -- see below), NOT computed by this repo from two independently reported counts, since the source does not report the underlying numerator count directly (see epic_n_patients_hepc_medication, which instead derives a count FROM this percent). The denominator (epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop) is ALL patients meeting the same viral hepatitis C diagnosis criteria as epic_n_patients_hepc (confirmed to match it cell-for-cell as of the 2026-09-10 update) -- NOT a smaller already-medicated subset. The measure is: percent of these patients with 1 slice by any of a named set of HCV antiviral medications (ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, sofosbuvir, elbasvir/grazoprevir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir) within 6 months of their diagnosis -- i.e. a treatment-initiation rate, as stated in the SlicerDicer session title. This is a SUBSTANTIVE DEFINITION CHANGE from the predecessor session (2850012): that session's rate (nationally 77-84 percent) was computed among an already-medicated subgroup and its exact clinical meaning was never confirmed; this session's rate is computed among all diagnosed patients and is explicitly a within-6-months treatment-initiation rate, so it is much lower in magnitude (nationally 14.5-17.5 percent, 2018-2025, trending upward) and NOT comparable to the old values -- do not chart them as a continuous series across this update. Where the underlying count was suppressed (10 or fewer, or a rate withheld even though the population was shown), the imputed rate is 5 / denominator * 100 and the cell is flagged by epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag. Where the denominator itself was suppressed, the value is left missing instead of computing 5 / 5 = 100%. The most recent period may be a partial year (currently 2026-07-28, narrower than epic_n_patients_hepc's own 2026-08-18 partial); use this percentage rather than the derived count for trend comparisons spanning the partial period, for the same reason described under epic_pct_hepc.

info.short_name: New HCV diagnoses
info.long_name: Number of patients newly diagnosed with hepatitis C (no diagnosis in the prior year)
info.short_description: Annual count of NEW (incident) hepatitis C diagnoses -- patients diagnosed in the given year who were not already diagnosed the year before -- in the 5 geographies with any exported data.
info.long_description: Taken from a dedicated, consolidated SlicerDicer session (2857569) that reports 6 measures at once (this population size, plus 5 rates -- see epic_pct_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis, epic_pct_hepc_abnormal_test_after_diagnosis, epic_pct_hepc_any_test_after_diagnosis, epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_diagnosis, epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_abnormal_new_diagnosis) cross-tabulated by state/year AND two additional row-bucket dimensions, (All) Lab Components in {"Hep C tests", Total} and All Medications in {"Hep C meds", Total}. Only the fully-unconditioned (Total x Total) row is kept here, per explicit user direction. The population is patients with a hepatitis C diagnosis in the given year who did NOT have one in the PRIOR year -- i.e. new/incident diagnoses, not the cumulative/prevalent diagnosed population -- confirmed with the user. This is why it is markedly smaller than epic_n_patients_hepc (crosstab 1, the cumulative diagnosed population as of that year: roughly 12-35% of it nationally, varying by year) and why it declines toward the present (167,148 nationally in 2018 down to 64,861 in 2025) even as epic_n_patients_hepc grows over the same span (471,746 to 561,496): fewer NEW diagnoses each year, while the prevalent pool keeps accumulating. Do not treat this as comparable to epic_n_patients_hepc or epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop -- it is a different (smaller, incident) population entirely. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed and imputed as 5, flagged by epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis_suppressed_flag. The most recent period (2026, partial year Jan 1 - Sep 1) is suppressed in EVERY one of the 5 geographies for this measure and all 5 percentage measures built on it -- confirmed directly in the raw export (every cell reads blank or "10 or fewer"), consistent with a partial year producing fewer new diagnoses than a full year, on top of the declining incidence trend.

epic_cosmos.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_cosmos.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from over 300 million patients across more than 1,600 hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems. Data is accessed via SlicerDicer, a self-service analytics tool. The dataset includes emergency department visits, diagnoses, immunizations, laboratory results, and other clinical data. Due to privacy protections, counts fewer than 10 are suppressed and imputed. Coverage extends across all U.S. states and territories. Note that county-level and city-level stratifications could differ markedly in total sample size due to high levels of missingness of county data in some states.
epic_cosmos.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'
